chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O Ali! Whoever loves you and then dies, he has fulfilled his destiny; and whoever loves you and has not yet died, he is awaiting [his turn]. And the sun does not rise nor set except that it brings him sustenance and faith; and in another copy, [it brings him] light.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for those who love Imam Ali (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the concept of 'wala' (loyalty) to Ali ibn Abi Talib as a means of spiritual sustenance and destiny fulfillment, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the Prophet's declaration of his love for Ali as a criterion for salvation. The mention of daily 'rizq' (sustenance) and 'iman' (faith) or 'nur' (light) underscores the continuous divine grace bestowed upon his lovers, a theme often linked to the spiritual authority (Wilayah) of the Ahl al-Bayt in Shia exegesis.

en.hubeali: H 14923 – A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al-Ashary, from Abdullah Bin Maymoun Al-Qaddaah, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullahasws has said that the Rasool Allahsaww said: ‘O Aliasws!

The one who loves you<sup>asws</sup>, then dies, so he has died. And the one who loves you<sup>asws</sup> and has not died yet, so he is awaiting. And the sun does not rise nor sets except that it comes to him with sustenance and the faith’. And in another copy (it says): ‘Light’.
en.sarwar: 476. Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nowfaly, from Al-Sakuny, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullah (a.s.) has said that the Rasool Allah (saww) said:

‘There will come a time upon my (saww) community when they will be ugly in their inner selves and beautiful in their appearances. They will be greedy for what is in the world and will not be intending what is in the Presence of Allah (azwj), their Lord (azwj). Their Religion would have become a (matter of) show-off. Fear will not have entered into them. Allah (azwj) would Prevail over them with Punishment. So they would be supplicating by the supplication of the Drowning One (Du’a Al-Ghareek), so He (azwj) will not Answer to them’.
